content: The Hebrew word 'bara' (בָּרָא) is used exclusively of God's creative activity. It implies bringing something entirely new into existence — not reshaping what was already there, but calling into being what had never been. This is the first truth of Scripture: before anything else, God was, and He made.
author: LLT Insight

content: The Spirit 'hovering' uses the Hebrew 'merachefet' — the same word used of an eagle stirring over its nest (Deut. 32:11). Even before light, before order, the Spirit was brooding over chaos with the tenderness of a parent. Darkness was not absence — it was anticipation.
author: LLT Insight

content: God speaks, and reality obeys. The pattern of creation by word echoes throughout Scripture: 'By the word of the LORD the heavens were made' (Psalm 33:6). John's Gospel opens with the same truth: 'In the beginning was the Word.' Creation is God's first sermon.
author: LLT Insight

content: 'Let us make man in our image' — the plural has stirred centuries of reflection. Early rabbis saw the divine council; the Church Fathers saw the Trinity. What's unmistakable is the deliberation: God pauses before creating humanity. Every other act was a command; this one is a conversation.
author: LLT Insight

content: The 'image of God' (imago Dei) is the cornerstone of human dignity. It doesn't point to physical resemblance but to the capacity for relationship, moral reasoning, and creative purpose. Every person you meet bears this mark — the fingerprint of the divine.
author: LLT Insight

content: Six times God called His work 'good.' But after creating humanity, He called it 'very good.' The Hebrew 'tov me'od' carries a sense of delight — this was not merely adequate. It was exactly what He wanted. You were exactly what He wanted.
author: LLT Insight
